whyWrong.au: au (à + le) is masculine — pharmacie is feminine: à la.
whyWrong.à l': à l' is used before a vowel or silent h — pharmacie starts with a consonant.
whyWrong.aux: aux (à + les) is plural — pharmacie is singular: à la.

whyWrong.à la: à la is feminine — marché is masculine: au.
whyWrong.à l': à l' is used before a vowel or silent h — marché starts with a consonant.
whyWrong.aux: aux (à + les) is plural — marché is singular: au.

whyWrong.du: du (de + le) is for masculine nouns after a consonant — hôpital has a silent h, so de l'.
whyWrong.de la: de la is feminine before a consonant — hôpital takes de l' before its vowel sound.
whyWrong.des: des (de + les) is plural — hôpital is singular: de l'.

whyWrong.au: au is masculine before a consonant — hôtel has a silent h, so à l'.
whyWrong.à la: à la is feminine before a consonant — hôtel takes à l' before its vowel sound.
whyWrong.aux: aux (à + les) is plural — hôtel is singular: à l'.

whyWrong.de la: de la is feminine — restaurant is masculine: du.
whyWrong.de l': de l' is used before a vowel or silent h — restaurant starts with a consonant.
whyWrong.de: plain de leaves out the article — a masculine noun needs du (de + le).
